nodes.name: ZIF-8 coated MoO3 carbonization
nodes.procedure: 0.20 g MoO3 and 0.59 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O were added into 20 mL methanol and evenly mixed. 0.82 g 2-Methylimidazole was dissolved into 20 mL methanol and added into the above solution, and then the mixed solution was filtered after it was stirred continuously for 3 h. The obtained powder dried at 80°C for overnight, and then the ZIF-8 coated MoO3 was heat-treated at 800°C for 2 h with a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹ under an Ar atmosphere. The products were cleaned several times by 0.1 mol/L HCl and deionized water, and then dried at 80°C for overnight, which was named as Mo2C-N.
nodes.source_text: 2.1. Preparation of Mo2C-N ... The Mo2C-N was obtained by a facile high temperature carbonization process ... which was named as Mo2C-N.

nodes.name: Melamine MoO3 carbonization
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g melamine and 1 g MoO3 were mixed well. The precursor was then calcined at 10°C·min⁻¹ in a tube furnace at Ar atmosphere 800 °C for 3 h to obtain a black solid powder MoO2@C.
nodes.source_text: The MoO2@C was synthesized by the controlling phase conversion. Typically, 0.5 g melamine and 1 g MoO3 were mixed well...

nodes.name: Ultrasound-assisted ZIS growth
nodes.procedure: A certain amount of Mo2C-N was added into 100 mL of deionized water, and then ultrasound for 1 h. Next, 0.119 g Zn(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.235 g InCl3·4H2O and 0.12 g TAA were dissolved into above mixed solution. The mixed solution was stirred for 30 min, and then was transferred into an oil bath at 100°C for 3 h. The Mo2C-N/ZIS powder was cleaned by centrifugation at 4000 rpm for 5 min. And then, the powder was dried at 80°C for overnight. The mass ratios of Mo2C-N to ZIS were 5%, 10%, 20%, denoted as 5-Mo2C-N/ZIS, 10-Mo2C-N/ZIS, 20-Mo2C-N/ZIS, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of obtained samples shows two sets of diffraction peaks corresponding to hexagonal ZIS (JCPDS #. 65-2023) and Mo₂C-N (JCPDS #. 65-8766).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of obtained samples shows two sets of diffraction peaks corresponding to hexagonal ZIS (JCPDS #. 65-2023) and Mo₂C-N (JCPDS #. 65-8766) (Fig. 1(d))

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Mo₂C-N exhibits abundant microscopic pore structure constructed when calcined at high temperature and Ar atmosphere.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surprisingly, abundant microscopic pore structure was constructed when calcined at high temperature and Ar atmosphere (Fig. 2(a-b)), indicating microscopic morphology and active sites can be modulated by phase change processes and carbon sources.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images display ZIS porous flower-like self-assembles from ultrathin 2D nanosheets uniformly encapsulating on 2D Mo₂C-N surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images further display that ZIS porous flower-like self-assembles from ultrathin two-dimensional (2D) nanosheets, which uniformly encapsulates on the surface of 2D Mo₂C-N

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM demonstrates lattice fringe distance of 0.23 nm attributed to ZIS (108) facet, and 0.24 nm attributed to Mo₂C-N (002) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3(d-f), the high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) demonstrates that the clear and tidy lattice fringe with distance of 0.23 nm can be attributed to ZIS (108) facet, and 0.24 nm attributed to Mo₂C-N (002) facet

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of ZIS, Mo₂C-N and 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS calculated to be 54.15 cm²/g, 5.57 cm²/g and 63.85 cm²/g respectively; nanopores center at 3.38 nm and 16 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area (BET) and pore-size distribution were tested... The BET surface area of ZIS, Mo₂C-N and 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS were calculated to be 54.15 cm²/g, 5.57 cm²/g and 63.85 cm²/g, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows Mo-C band detected in Mo₂C-N; peaks at 568, 874 and 998 cm⁻¹ correspond to Mo=O, Mo-O-Mo and Mo=O bands in α-MoO₃ samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform-infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) of as-prepared samples was shown in Fig. S6(e-f). The Mo-C band was detected in the FTIR curve of Mo₂C-N

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum shows peaks at 245, 306 and 349 cm⁻¹ ascribed to A₂g, Eg, A₁g active modes of ZIS; peaks at 279, 817, 991 cm⁻¹ and 567 cm⁻¹ for Mo-C bands of Mo₂C-N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, in Raman spectrum of ZIS and Mo₂C-N/ZIS, the peaks appeared at 245, 306 and 349 cm⁻¹ are ascribed to A₂g, Eg, A₁g active modes of ZIS, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo 3d peaks at 231.5, 232.5, 233.1, 233.7 and 235.9 eV assigned to Mo⁰, Mo²⁺, Mo⁶⁺, Mo⁴⁺, Mo²⁺; binding energy shifts toward higher energy after ZIS growth; N 1s peaks at 396.0, 397.7, 399.0, 401.1 eV for Mo-N, pyridinic N, pyrrolic N, graphitic N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was carried out to further evaluate the chemical composition and valence states... For the Mo 3d XPS spectra, Mo in various valence states exists in Mo₂C-N samples, the peaks at 231.5, 232.5, 233.1, 233.7 and 235.9 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping revealed even distribution of Mo, C, N, Zn, In and S in the circled part of 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS image.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, energy-dispersive Xray (EDS) mapping revealed an even distribution of Mo, C, and N, respectively (Fig. S3). Likewise, the distribution of Mo, C, N, Zn, In and S in Mo₂C-N/ZIS was also confirmed for Mo₂C-N and ZIS (Fig. 2(i-n) and Fig. S4(d-i)).

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis DRS shows Mo₂C-N/ZIS Schottky junction has enhanced visible-light absorption compared to ZIS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV–vis diffuse reflectance spectra (DRS) demonstrated that... The Mo₂C-N/ZIS Schottky junction sandwich nanostructured shows an enhanced visible-light absorption than that of ZIS

nodes.characterization_summary: Mott-Schottky plots give flat-band potentials of ZIS (-0.77 eV), Mo₂C-N (-0.12 eV), 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS (-0.31 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, it is notable that the conduction band (CB) and valence band (VB) positions of the obtained samples are determined by Mott-Schottky plots. The flat-band potentials of ZIS, Mo₂C-N, 5-Mo₂C-N/ZIS, 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS, 20-Mo₂C-N/ZIS

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives double-layer capacitance Cdl of 2.76 mF·cm⁻² and ECSA of 69.00 cm² for 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS, higher than ZIS and Mo₂C-N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, the 10-Mo₂C-N/ZIS catalyst exhibits the highest Cdl value of 2.76 mF·cm⁻² and largest ECSA value of 69.00 cm² (Fig. S13-14).
